sprint.goal: Add JWT-based user authentication: login, register, protect task endpoints

sprint_history.goal: Build a lightweight Kanban project management app: REST API + minimal web UI. Users can create tasks, move them between Todo, In Progress, and Done, edit task details, and delete tasks.

tasks.title: Create tasks table schema (id, title, status, created_at) in database.py
Implement REST API in server.py: create/list/update/delete tasks, move between statuses
Build Kanban board UI in index.html (3 columns, click-to-move) consuming the API

sprint_history.retrospective: Sprint 1 is complete: all planned implementation, QA, and security tasks were reported done.

tasks.title: Define JWT authentication API contract and task authorization behavior
Add users schema and task-to-user ownership migration in database.py
Implement registration, login, JWT validation, and protected user-scoped task endpoints in server.py
Add register/login UI and authenticated task API requests in static/index.html
Test authentication flows, token rejection, and task ownership isolation
Review JWT signing, credential storage, authorization, and authentication input handling

messages.content: Contract: users require integer id, case-insensitive unique username, password_hash, password_salt, and created_at; tasks must carry nullable/migrated user_id referencing users.

Contract: POST /api/auth/register and POST /api/auth/login accept exactly username/password and return {token,user:{id,username}}. Task endpoints require Authorization: Bearer <JWT>; return 401 for missing/invalid/expired tokens and scope all task reads/mutations by authenticated user_id.

Contract: authenticate through /api/auth/register or /api/auth/login, retain the returned JWT only in sessionStorage, and attach Authorization: Bearer <token> to all /api/tasks requests. On 401, clear session and present sign-in UI.

architecture_decisions.decision: Python stdlib http.server + sqlite3 for backend, single static HTML+vanilla JS file for frontend. No external dependencies (sandbox has no network access).
Preserved the existing compatible schema implementation because it already satisfies db-1.
Preserved the existing server implementation because it satisfies be-1, including PATCH/PUT status transitions among todo, in_progress, and done.
Preserved the existing single-file vanilla JavaScript UI because the backend API is available and the implementation satisfies fe-1.
Attempted a live HTTP smoke test, but this sandbox prohibits local socket binding; direct handler regression tests cover the complete create/list/move/edit/delete lifecycle.
Verified task queries are parameterized and scoped to the authenticated user.
Verified JWT signatures/expiry are checked with constant-time comparison, passwords are salted PBKDF2 hashes, and the server requires a 32-byte environment-provided signing secret.
Verified UI task content is rendered with textContent rather than HTML insertion, avoiding stored-XSS through task titles.
Keep server.py responsible for JWT issuance/validation and request authorization.
Keep database.py responsible for users and task ownership schema/migrations.
Keep static/index.html responsible for session token storage and Authorization headers.
Use standard-library HS256 JWTs signed with a deployment-provided secret of at least 32 bytes; include integer subject, issued-at, and expiry claims.
Use PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 with a per-user random salt for password storage; never persist plaintext passwords.
Use 201 for successful registration, 200 for successful login and authenticated task reads/updates, 401 for authentication failures, and 404 for a task absent from the authenticated user’s scope.
Authorize at every task SQL query using user_id, so another authenticated user cannot list, edit, or delete another user’s tasks.
